name: Rama
role: Prince of Ayodhya and the hero of the Ramayana, honoured as the seventh avatara of Vishnu and as an embodiment of dharma.
fun_fact: Rama's story is retold in dozens of languages, and the chanting of his name is an everyday devotional practice for millions of people.

name: Sita
role: Wife of Rama and queen of Ayodhya, daughter of King Janaka, and in many traditions an avatara of the goddess Lakshmi.
fun_fact: Her name is traditionally linked to the Sanskrit word sita, meaning furrow, because she was said to have been found in a ploughed field.

name: Hanuman
role: Vanara hero and devoted servant of Rama, famous for his strength, his leap to Lanka and his unwavering loyalty.
fun_fact: Hanuman is counted among the Chiranjivis, beings said to remain alive through the ages, and he is honoured at gyms and wrestling halls across India.

name: Ravana
role: Ten-headed king of Lanka, a learned and powerful rakshasa who abducts Sita and is finally defeated by Rama.
fun_fact: Tradition remembers Ravana as a great scholar and devotee of Shiva, and hymns such as the Shiva Tandava Stotram are attributed to him.

name: Krishna
role: The eighth avatara of Vishnu, Arjuna's charioteer and teacher in the Bhagavad Gita, and the beloved child of Vrindavan.
fun_fact: Krishna's childhood pranks, his flute and his butter theft are told with affection in the Bhagavata Purana and in poetry across India.

name: Arjuna
role: The third of the five Pandava brothers and the greatest archer of the Mahabharata, who receives Krishna's teaching on the battlefield.
fun_fact: Arjuna's bow is called Gandiva, and he is often given the epithet Savyasachin, the one who can shoot with either hand.

name: Durga
role: Warrior goddess who defeats Mahishasura, honoured as a form of the great Goddess and as a protector of the worlds.
fun_fact: Durga is celebrated in the nine-night festival of Navaratri, and her autumn worship is especially elaborate in Bengal's Durga Puja.

name: Vishnu
role: One of the great gods, the preserver who sustains the world and takes avatara forms such as Rama, Krishna and the tortoise Kurma.
fun_fact: Vishnu's avatars are commonly counted as ten, and the tenth, Kalki, is expected to appear in a future age.

name: Lakshmana
role: Rama's younger brother and constant companion in exile, whose loyalty carries him through the forest and the war in Lanka.
fun_fact: Lakshmana is traditionally identified as an incarnation of Shesha, the great serpent on whom Vishnu rests.

name: Mahishasura
role: Buffalo demon whose boon and conquests prompt the gods to create Durga, who ends his rule.
fun_fact: His name comes from mahisha, the Sanskrit word for buffalo, and his defeat is recalled each year during Navaratri.
